text:
maya patel: Quick sync — need ordering input for Optimize toolkit (quantization, batching, caching). Customer signals and launch constraints coming in; who thinks RICE helps decide?

alex kim: did a fast pass. My gut: quantization -> batching -> caching for cost wins. But caching often wins for latency-sensitive online routes.

sam rodriguez: +1 on that split. Enterprise customer A will churn if tail latency stays high even with cost savings. They care about p95 more than $/token.

alex kim: rough RICE sketch (very quick):
```
Feature      Reach Impact Confidence Effort  RICE
Quantization  8/10  6/10    7/10       3      112
Batching      7/10  5/10    6/10       4       52
Caching       5/10  8/10    6/10       5       48
```
Numbers are normalized-ish, not final — shows quant looks best for raw ROI but caching = high impact for latency.

lisa nguyen: Suggest we don't treat this as one linear backlog item. Propose two parallel launch tracks:
- cost-first: quant + batch optimizations, target unit cost drop and docs for migrations
- latency-first: prefix/KV caching + light quant to avoid quality regression

denise (pm): launch criteria proposals:
- cost-first: >=20% cost/unit reduction on common LLMs, p95 <= 200ms for standard short prompts, integration docs, migration guide
- latency-first: p95 <= 120ms for targeted online routes, cache hit >= 80% on warm prefixes, no quality regression > 2% on eval set
Also require canary plan and rollback criteria.

alex kim: important engineering note: aggressive quantization changes KV cache bit patterns and may alter effective cache hit behavior. Need a small eval matrix: quality delta, cache hit delta, latency change across seq lengths.

maya patel: can we scope a tech spike: quant on 13B family (int8), measure quality delta on 500 prompt eval set, latency & cost? Also sample cache sim to estimate effectiveness for our top-10 routes.

sam rodriguez: customer A (dedicated) also flagged batching as high priority — they want predictable throughput under steady load. That could shift sequencing if Dedicated contracts drive revenue.

ci-bot: REMINDER: Optimize toolkit sync tomorrow 10:00am PT.

lisa nguyen: we should add explicit rollback triggers:
- eval quality regression > 2% on critical prompt set
- error rate increase > 1%
- user-reported latencies increase above SLA for 10m window

denise (pm): next steps: alex + sam to draft tech-spike plan with perf matrix and effort estimates by EOD Friday. I'll consolidate customer asks and finalize RICE worksheet before Monday.

maya patel: :thumbsup: thanks. Bring blockers to the sync or DM me.
